rules.banned_because: Someone else's names, kept out of everything Euphonia publishes (Appendix E; setting/ip-review.md).
rules.fey_type_because: "Fey" survives only as the creature type; the setting's prose says "fae" (Book Two, What's Different). The 2024 rules' own names keep it too: Fey Ancestry, Fey Touched, Fey Wanderer, Summon Fey and the SRD's Conjure Fey (Chat, 15 November). So does a list of creature types: "any Undead, Fey, or Elemental".
rules.renames_because: The setting's own names for those planes, the first two of the Revelator's Cosmography: the Feywild is the Hidden, the Shadowfell the Ghostlands (setting/whats-out.md, wheel-and-plenum.md). The SRD's "the Feywild" reads "the Hidden".

backgrounds.name: Company Factor
backgrounds.equipment: Choose A or B: (A) Navigator's Tools, Traveler's Clothes, Ink, Ink Pen, 10 sheets of Parchment, Lamp, Pouch, 10 GP; or (B) 50 GP
backgrounds.about: You kept a company's books at a factory, as a trading post is called, and learned that a company is a state that happens to float: it makes treaties, builds forts and keeps an army. You've dealt with kings, sultans and pirates and dropped each when the books said so, and you know what a Mutapan lamp fetches in three currencies. The house may as easily have been a Gujarati one in Surat or a Swahili one in Mombasa as the VOC; a factory's books read the same in any script. Counsellors (the Factor), Rogues and Wizards on company contracts come from here.
backgrounds.door: Any company's factory or counting house in a port opens its books to you and finds you a bed.
backgrounds.debt: Your old employers want you back, and Mutapa's spymaster keeps a file on you.

backgrounds.name: Court Creature
backgrounds.equipment: Choose A or B: (A) Fine Clothes, Gaming Set (playing cards), Perfume, Signet Ring (5 GP), Dagger, Sealing Wax (5 SP), Ink, Ink Pen, 5 sheets of Parchment, 11 GP; or (B) 50 GP
backgrounds.about: You grew up in a household that lived by a license: a court wizard's royal patent, or a minor noble's place at court. You carried the letters, sat at the gaming tables where posts are won and lost, and learned who was about to fall before they did. You can read a room, forge a seal in a pinch and tell last year's lace from this year's, and the Children of the Emerald Tablet know your face. Counsellors, Wizards and Eldritch Knights (*Player's Handbook*) come out of these houses.
backgrounds.door: The house that raised you gets you into its court, and its servants still talk to you.
backgrounds.debt: Whoever holds that house's license now owns a piece of you, and your court's spymaster knows your debts.

backgrounds.name: Cunning Folk
backgrounds.equipment: Choose A or B: (A) Herbalism Kit, Healer's Kit, Quarterstaff, Book (charms and receipts), Traveler's Clothes, 10 Candles, Pouch, 12 GP; or (B) 50 GP
backgrounds.about: You healed, found lost things and charmed warts and cattle out of the back room of a family business, because somebody had to. England calls your kind cunning folk; New Spain says curandero, and Kongo nganga. Like most of your kind, you read; in England the law has let unlicensed herb-knowers treat external complaints since 1542. Your magic is Lanternhall's, without its protection: when a healer tells a court her skill came from the fairies, the court writes down the Devil. Your clients live at the edge, so you know the border too (the Hidden Domain, in *Life on the Border*). Druids, Clerics and Physicians who skipped the hospital come from here; the Physician's Hedge Witch is the model.
backgrounds.door: Your network knows who's safe and who's informing in any district, and hides its own.
backgrounds.debt: You're unlicensed, and someone can prove it.

backgrounds.name: Schooled
backgrounds.feat: Magic Initiate (Cleric or Wizard, your choice)
backgrounds.equipment: Choose A or B: (A) Calligrapher's Supplies, Book (your school's), 8 sheets of Parchment, Robe, Lamp, Oil, Quarterstaff, 12 GP; or (B) 50 GP
backgrounds.about: Choose the institution. The Society of Jesus runs hundreds of colleges on one printed curriculum, the *Ratio Studiorum* of 1599. A seminary made you a priest's assistant who can argue a point. A madrasa in Bukhara, Cairo or Timbuktu taught you the science of letters alongside the law. A university or an academy made you a natural philosopher's apprentice, and the Children of the Emerald Tablet who taught you now count you an enemy. Whichever it was, you read three languages and dispute in one, and the Republic of Letters wants your correspondence. Wizards, Clerics, Natural Philosophers, Counsellors and Physicians are schooled this way.
backgrounds.door: Your letters get answered across a war, and any college of your order gives you a room and a library.
backgrounds.debt: Your school's masters (the Society of Jesus, a bishop, a madrasa's teachers or a university's chair) want your loyalty, and every spymaster reads your post.

backgrounds.name: Mutapan Agent
backgrounds.equipment: Choose A or B: (A) Tinker's Tools; or (B) 50 GP
backgrounds.about: You work abroad for Mutapa, under the cover it gives its people: a Mhizha taught you to retune curiosities (Mutapan Curiosities, below). Every Mutapan lamp in a Viennese drawing room drifts, so a quiet technician with Tinker's Tools enters any great house in Europe and is thanked for it. What you carry home is what you saw. Mutapa's spymaster is brilliant and badly resourced, and her service runs on people like you. You may be a Shona clerk of the House of the Bird (Mutapa's bank), a Khoekhoe go-between from Hoerikwaggo or a foreigner recruited at Sofala; loyal, bought or both. Mhizha, Counsellors and Rogues come this way.
backgrounds.door: Any house that owns a curiosity lets you in to retune it, and thanks you.

backgrounds.name: Buccaneer
backgrounds.equipment: Choose A or B: (A) Light Crossbow, 20 Bolts, Handaxe, Dagger, Cook's Utensils, Traveler's Clothes, Rope, 13 GP; or (B) 50 GP
backgrounds.about: You signed articles. Before every cruise the Brethren of the Coast at Port Royal and Tortuga write the terms: the captain's share, the surgeon's, a payment set down for each limb or eye lost, and no prey, no pay. You voted on the captain and smoked beef over a boucan, which is where the name comes from. No license sails with the Brethren, and the witch who can raise a wind draws a full share. Fighters, Rogues, Rangers and Storm Sorcerers come off these ships, and the odd Cleric who found the Brethren more honest than the bishop.
backgrounds.door: Any free port's taverns know the articles you signed, and a crew there will take you on.
backgrounds.debt: Spain wants you hanged, and every governor who used you will eventually agree.

backgrounds.name: Veteran of the German Wars
backgrounds.equipment: Choose A or B: (A) Spear, Shortsword, Carpenter's Tools, Leather Armor, Shovel, Healer's Kit, Traveler's Clothes, Bedroll, 11 GP; or (B) 50 GP
backgrounds.about: You were in the Empire's war of 1618 to 1648, when every crown in Europe fought over German ground and the war fed on the villages it crossed. You fought at Breitenfeld or Lützen, or were a child the army took along, and the peace sent you home to find no home. Your trade is the one the war taught: drill by numbers, dig in, build the palisade, keep the men fed. If you're young for it, you learned it in Portugal's war, on Candia's walls or on the Andean front, on either side of it. Fighters above all, Battle Masters (*Player's Handbook*) in particular; Barbarians who found the rage in a breach; Clerics who buried too many; the Natural Philosopher who learned ballistics from a gunner.
backgrounds.door: Any mercenary colonel's camp feeds you, and most will hire you.
backgrounds.debt: The Agitators think you owe the villages the war ate, and they've come to collect.

backgrounds.name: Border-Born
backgrounds.equipment: Choose A or B: (A) Smith's Tools, Sling, 20 Sling Bullets, Dagger, Hunting Trap, 10 Iron Spikes, Hooded Lantern, Oil, Traveler's Clothes, Pouch of salt (1 CP), 14 GP; or (B) 50 GP
backgrounds.about: You grew up where the Hidden come over. The village ironed and salted its doors every night of the dark half; the smith was the most important person in it, and you were her hand. You know the tide by the moon, which fields nobody plows and why the fiddler who came home last spring is a hundred years out of date. You sleep light: you were indoors before the last open night because you heard it coming. You may have grown up on either side of the border (*Life on the Border*), and your country's name for the Hidden is in The State of the World. In the courts, you notice when the iron is missing from the doorframe.
backgrounds.door: Any border village takes you in and asks you to look at its doors.
backgrounds.debt: Somebody you knew was taken, and nobody has brought them back.

backgrounds.name: Taken
backgrounds.tool: Choose one kind of Musical Instrument
backgrounds.equipment: Choose A or B: (A) Musical Instrument (same as above), Traveler's Clothes, Bedroll, Tinderbox, Pouch, 34 GP; or (B) 50 GP
backgrounds.about: The Hidden took you, and you came home. Maybe you were a child and they left something in your cradle; maybe you followed music into a hill on your way back from market. You remember a feast, a dance that lasted a night and a road that kept turning back, and none of it in order. Home had moved on without you: a week, a year or a hundred, and the people who mourned you are older, or dead, or sure you're not you. You came back with a tune nobody taught you, a knack for hedge-magic and the habit of looking for the way out of every room. Whether you carry a piece of the Hidden is settled by your class (*Life on the Border*, Introduction); a Rogue taken as a child may simply be quick and strange. Your country's word for the taken is in The State of the World.
backgrounds.door: The Hidden of one court know you by sight, and will parley with you where they'd raid anyone else.
backgrounds.debt: Something there still wants you back.

backgrounds.name: Noble
backgrounds.tool: Choose one kind of Gaming Set
backgrounds.equipment: Choose A or B: (A) Gaming Set (same as above), Fine Clothes, Perfume, Mirror, Dagger, Chest, Lock, 7 GP; or (B) 50 GP
backgrounds.about: You were born into a house that holds rank: a Castilian grandee's or a Rajput chief's title and land, one of the titled houses of Benin City or a noble house of Kongo, a chiefly line on Tongatapu whose gifts reach Samoa and Fiji, or a Haudenosaunee lineage that holds one of the League's titles, whose clan mother chooses who carries it. Rank in 1668 is a set of duties as much as a privilege: you were raised to host, to judge, to give the gift that binds and to remember what every other house owes yours. A woman can head any house in this book. Courtiers, Paladins, Fighters and Counsellors come from these houses, and so do the Clerics a family gives to its church, mosque or temple.
backgrounds.door: Any house of your rank receives you as a guest, and its head will hear what you came to say.
backgrounds.debt: Your family expects you to win back what it has lost, and a rival house is waiting for you to fail.

backgrounds.name: Artisan
backgrounds.tool: Choose one kind of Artisan's Tools
backgrounds.equipment: Choose A or B: (A) Artisan's Tools (same as above), Traveler's Clothes, 2 Pouches, 37 GP; or (B) 50 GP
backgrounds.about: You learned a craft at someone's bench. In London or Florence that meant seven years' apprenticeship and a guild's leave to open a shop; in Benin City, a place in one of the king's guilds, such as the brass casters'; in Gujarat, a family's looms; in Edo, a master's house and, one day, its name; in Sofala, a Mhizha's workshop. You can tell whose hand made a thing by looking at the joins. A craft is a license of its own kind: a guild or a master decides who may set up shop, and work that carries magic answers to the licensing courts as well. A woman can hold any trade and its mastership. Natural Philosophers who build their own instruments, Mhizha, Physicians who learned surgery as a craft and Courtiers of the College of Art come from here, and so does the Hidden Killer who forges her own iron.
backgrounds.door: Any workshop of your craft gives you a bench and a meal, and its people talk shop with you.
backgrounds.debt: Your old master's house says you still owe it years or a share, and a rival shop wants your secrets.

backgrounds.name: Merchant
backgrounds.equipment: Choose A or B: (A) Navigator's Tools, Mule, Traveler's Clothes, Rope, Lamp, Pouch, 13 GP; or (B) 50 GP
backgrounds.about: You trade on your own account or your family's: a stall in a Yoruba market town, where the market is women's business; a caravan between Bukhara and Astrakhan; a share in a ship on the Monsoon Road; or money lent from a cloth spread in a caravanserai. No company answers for you, only your partners and the paper you've signed (a company's man takes Company Factor instead). Credit is the whole trade: a bill written in Surat is paid in Isfahan because your name is on it, and a name lost in one market is lost in all of them. Counsellors (the Factor and the Gamester above all), Clerics who keep a market's shrine and Sorcerers who sail come from here.
backgrounds.door: Any market or caravanserai on your routes knows your name, and someone there will give you credit.
backgrounds.debt: A creditor holds your paper, and a rival would like to see it called in.

backgrounds.name: Entertainer
backgrounds.tool: Choose one kind of Musical Instrument
backgrounds.equipment: Choose A or B: (A) Musical Instrument (same as above), Costume, Mirror, Traveler's Clothes, Bedroll, Tinderbox, Pouch, 24 GP; or (B) 50 GP
backgrounds.about: You perform for a living: songs at weddings, stories in a coffeehouse, tumbling in a square, the mbira at an all-night bira where the ancestors are called, hula for a chief on Hawaiʻi, a Kazakh akyn's sung contest at the autumn pasture. In Venice the mountebanks of the Piazza San Marco sell cures between their acts, and gave Europe the word *charlatan*. Women perform everywhere, and since 1660 they have acted on London's stage as well as on those of Paris and Venice. Music is also the oldest road to the Hidden: the best players get asked to play for them, and some come back (Taken, above). Bards, Courtiers of the College of Verse, Warlocks whose patron heard them play, Danae who learned to cross roofs in front of a crowd and Barbarians who dance before they fight come from here.
backgrounds.door: Any fair, festival or great hall makes room for you, and the other performers there share their news and their supper.
backgrounds.debt: The troupe, the patron or the teacher who made you wants a share of everything you earn.

backgrounds.name: Retainer
backgrounds.equipment: Choose A or B: (A) Calligrapher's Supplies, Fine Clothes (your house's livery), Lock, Dagger, 10 sheets of Paper, Lamp, Pouch, 10 GP; or (B) 50 GP
backgrounds.about: You served a house (a court, a temple, a city's council, a merchant family or a lord's household) as its secretary, its steward or the guard at its gate. Every power in 1668 runs on people like you: the Ottoman chancery's scribes, a Chinese magistrate's clerks, the secretaries of Venice's Council of Ten, the khipukamayuq who keep the Inca state's accounts in knotted cords, the palace servants who carry the Alaafin's word through Oyo. You know where a house keeps its papers and who reads its post before it does. A license is a paper too, and you know which drawer it's in. Counsellors come from here more than from anywhere (the Spymaster, the Majordomo and the Marshal), and so do Wizards who began as copyists and Revelators who served a court of justice.
backgrounds.door: Any great household lets you in by the servants' door, and its people tell you who is rising and who is falling.
backgrounds.debt: The house you served expects your silence, and someone else will pay well to break it.

backgrounds.name: Guide
backgrounds.equipment: Choose A or B: (A) Navigator's Tools, Spear, Traveler's Clothes, Bedroll, Tent, Rope, Tinderbox, Pouch, 4 days of Rations, 15 GP; or (B) 50 GP
backgrounds.about: You know a stretch of the world well enough to take other people through it: the passes of the Hindu Kush, the portages between the Great Lakes and the rivers that run to the sea, the wells of a desert caravan road, the reefs from Pate to Sofala, or the star paths between Polowat and Pohnpei, held in the head with no instrument at all. The maps travelers carry home are mostly what you told them, with your name left off. You know which ground the people who live there leave alone, because the Hidden walk on it, and the hedge-magic every guide picks up: a word for the weather, a ward around the camp. Rangers and Druids come from here, and so do Revelators who walk roads nobody else can see and the Natural Philosopher who learned the stars from a navigator.
backgrounds.door: Any village, camp or harbor on the routes you know takes your word on the way ahead, and feeds you for news of it.
backgrounds.debt: Someone you once led didn't come back, and their family holds you to it.

backgrounds.name: Farmer
backgrounds.equipment: Choose A or B: (A) Carpenter's Tools, Sickle, Shovel, Iron Pot, Traveler's Clothes, Blanket, Rope, Pouch, 33 GP; or (B) 50 GP
backgrounds.about: Most people in 1668 farm, herd or fish, and you are one of them. You may have grown yams on Pohnpei, rice on Formosa's east coast, millet on Mutapa's plateau, maize and beans in the fields of a Haudenosaunee town, which belong to its women, or wheat on the Dnieper for a lord who never saw it. Your day starts before light, which is why nothing in a camp gets past you, and you know which field the village leaves for the Hidden and what to set on the step on the open nights. A bad harvest is a war, a tax or a curse, and you've lived through all three. Druids and Clerics of the harvest come from here, and so do Barbarians and Fighters who left the farm for a war and the Counsellor who runs a household's granary as if it were a kingdom.
backgrounds.door: Any farming village takes you in for a day's work, and tells you what the landlord and the Hidden have been doing.
backgrounds.debt: Your family's land is owed to someone (a landlord, a lord, a temple or a moneylender), and the rent is due.

species.line: Everywhere, in every people's own words
Hearthfolk, with each culture's own name
Dragons are real, and a few bloodlines carry them. Where the dragon was a god, as on China's rivers, a dragonborn is a sign; where it was a monster, she keeps her sleeves down
Of the giants, which are among the shapes the Hidden took; a goliath's ancestors forgot the same way, though nobody counts a goliath among the hearthfolk

A people made by their own god, as the core books have them, with towns of their own in the hard high country between the empires; an orc in Venice or Delhi is a traveler from one of them. Not Hidden, and not anyone's soldiers

A fiendish mark from the hells. In a Europe that burns people for the Devil's pact, a tiefling is proof of a crime nobody committed; Spain's Inquisition, which demands evidence, is safer ground than a prince-bishop's court
Descended from an elemental being that crossed from one of the four elemental spheres in human shape and forgot. Its traits are in *A Player's Companion* (Species)

Divinity in the body, by one of two strands: descent from a god itself, through a line her people records (the Sun's line of the Sapa Inca, Amaterasu's of Japan's emperors), or the touch of a god's servants, the angel tier, in any tradition that has one (a Shinto shrine's priestess, a Kabbalist's child). Some are born holy. Its traits are in *A Player's Companion* (Species)

book_species.name: Elemental-Blood
book_species.lead: An elemental-blood descends from a being of one of the four elemental spheres that crossed into the world in human shape and in time forgot what it was (*The Setting*, Peoples, Elemental-Bloods). The blood is inherited, a thing about her body. She doesn't cast it, it doesn't build up in her and it never has to be let out, which is how anyone who knows the difference tells her from a sorcerer. Now and then the blood remembers the shape it came in.
book_species.size: Medium (about 4–7 feet tall) or Small (about 3–4 feet tall), chosen when you select this species

traits.name: Elemental Lineage
traits.text: Your forebear came from one of the four elemental spheres that wrap the world as the period draws it: earth at the center, then water, then air, then fire, just below the Moon. Choose a lineage from the Elemental Lineages table. You have Resistance to its damage type, and you have its level 1 trait.

traits.name: The Old Shape
traits.text: When you reach level 3, you can take a Bonus Action to let the blood remember the shape it crossed in. For 1 minute you take on a trace of it, by your lineage:

options.name: Earth: Stone
options.text: Your skin goes gray and hard as a quarry face. You gain a +2 bonus to Armor Class, and you have a Burrow Speed of 20 feet through earth and loose stone, though not worked stone; you leave no tunnel.

options.name: Water: The Current
options.text: You move like water. Whenever you take damage, reduce it by your Proficiency Bonus, and you can move through the space of any creature.

options.name: Air: The Wind
options.text: You are half wind. You have a Fly Speed equal to your Speed and can hover, and the first attack roll made against you each round has Disadvantage.

options.name: Fire: The Flame
options.text: You burn without being burned. You shed Bright Light in a 10-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 10 feet. Once on each of your turns, when you deal damage to a creature, it takes extra Fire damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and a creature that hits you with a melee attack takes Fire damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus.

traits.after: You can take the Old Shape once, and you regain the use when you finish a Long Rest. From level 5 you can take it twice between Long Rests. The trace can't be hidden while it lasts: anyone who sees it knows what you are, and a witch-finder writes it down.

traits.name: Kin of the Sphere
traits.text: Elementals of your lineage's sphere know you on sight for one of theirs who forgot. Knowing isn't liking: by default an elemental is curious and wary of you, and the DM can say otherwise.

traits.name: The Sphere's Knack
traits.text: You know the *Elementalism* cantrip, and you can use it only on your lineage's element. Intelligence, Wisdom or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for it (choose when you select this species). It isn't a learned spell: you have done it since you could walk, and no school taught it to you. Whether the law counts it as magic is a question every ministry answers differently (*The Setting*, Magic, Scarcity and Distance).

head: Lineage
What a learned European calls you
Resistance
Level 1 trait
rows: A pygmy, or a gnome, Paracelsus's other word, which the gnomes resent
**Rooted.** While you stand on earth or stone, you have Advantage on saving throws and ability checks to avoid being moved against your will or knocked Prone
**Of the Water.** You have a Swim Speed equal to your Speed, and you can hold your breath for 1 hour
**Light on the Air.** Your Speed is 35 feet, and the distance of your Long Jump and High Jump is doubled
**Kindled.** You have Darkvision with a range of 60 feet, and the Burning hazard doesn't affect you; you can hold a coal or a candle flame in your bare hand without harm

book_species.name: Divine-Blood
book_species.lead: A divine-blood carries a god's divinity in her body, by one of two strands: descent from the god itself, or the touch of its servants (*The Setting*, Peoples, Divine-Bloods). She did nothing to earn it. A Cleric earns power by devotion, a Warlock bargains for it and a Sorcerer vents a plane pushing through; a divine-blood just has it, by birth, and owes nothing for it. None of these traits is a spell, and none of them asks anything of her: the blood does them on its own.
book_species.size: Medium (about 4–7 feet tall) or Small (about 3–4 feet tall), chosen when you select this species

traits.name: Divine Strand
traits.text: Choose your strand: **the Line**, descent from the god itself through a line your people records, or **the Touch**, the touch of a god's servants, the messengers every heaven sends. You have the traits of your strand, below. One person can carry both strands; if your character does, choose one for its traits and describe the other.

traits.name: Known on Sight
traits.text: The god's spirits, servants and sacred animals know what you are when they see you, and its priests feel you come into a room. If you are angel-touched, the messengers of the heaven that touched you know you too. None of them is bound to like you, and the god's own people, if they see it, are the dangerous part.

traits.name: The God's Province
traits.text: A god forms where a people's faith meets a phenomenon or a system (*The Setting* tells how), and your god's province is in your blood. Choose it from the God's Provinces table; you have Resistance to its damage type. The province is courteous to you in small ways (*The Setting*, Peoples, Divine-Bloods, Playing a Divine-Blood).

traits.name: The Blood Refuses
traits.text: From level 3, when you fail a saving throw, you can succeed instead. Once this happens, it can't happen again until you finish a Long Rest. It isn't something you do: the blood won't have it.

traits.name: The Blood Shows
traits.text: From level 5, the first time you are Bloodied after a Long Rest, the blood shows. For a moment, everyone near you sees the god's province gather around you: the sun through a roof, the smell of rain, spray off nothing, heat, the hum of the ground. Each ally within 30 feet of you who can see you gains Temporary Hit Points equal to your level. Everyone who saw it knows what you are, and a court that claims your line will hear of it by evening.

traits.name: Born Holy
traits.text: You have Resistance to Radiant damage. You can shed Dim Light in a 5-foot radius, or put it out, at will and without an action; the light was in you when you were born.

traits.name: The Messenger's Hand
traits.text: When you fall, you descend 60 feet per round and take no damage from the fall, unless you have the Incapacitated condition. Something caught you once, and the air remembers.

traits.name: Caught Before the Fall
traits.text: From level 3, when a creature you can see within 30 feet of you drops to 0 Hit Points and isn't killed outright, you can take a Reaction to have it drop to 1 Hit Point instead. Once you do, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

traits.name: Borne Up
traits.text: From level 5, once per Long Rest, when you jump or fall, you can gain a Fly Speed equal to your Speed for 10 minutes. The messengers carried you this way once, and the touch remembers how.

Tangaloa's through the Tuʻi Tonga, Tengri's through Chinggis Khan, Wākea's through the Hawaiian aliʻi, Zeus's
**The sea, a river or the moon**
Nyikang's, whose mother is the river, through the Shilluk reth, Chandra's through the Rajput houses of the Moon, Poseidon's, Thetis's

Papahānaumoku's through the Hawaiian aliʻi, Oduduwa's through the Yoruba crowns

species_and_people.text: Every species takes its traits as written; the setting supplies where it comes from and what 1668 makes of it. Pick the species, then the people: where the family comes from, what that place calls them and what it thinks of them. The trouble comes with the country. The lore behind each is in Peoples.
species_and_people.where: The Setting, Characters, Species and People
